feature: gRPC TLS channels through authenticated SOCKS5

scope.proxy: RFC 1928 CONNECT with optional RFC 1929 username/password authentication
scope.origin_transport: certificate-verified TLS 1.3 with mandatory h2 ALPN
scope.dns: origin hostname is carried as a SOCKS domain target and is not resolved locally

standards: RFC 1929 Username/Password Authentication for SOCKS V5

grpc_core.audit: case-insensitive source search found only c-ares socket variable names, not a SOCKS proxy transport

observed_contract: proxy routing and credentials are independent from origin TLS and gRPC identity
one absolute attempt deadline spans proxy resolution, TCP, authentication, CONNECT, TLS, ALPN, and HTTP2 bootstrap
proxy-side DNS requires the untouched origin hostname in the SOCKS request
a persistent HTTP2 connection reuses one successful SOCKS tunnel across later gRPC streams

implementation.endpoint: tls_host accepts optional ChannelSocks5Proxy and rejects simultaneous HTTP CONNECT plus SOCKS configuration
implementation.validation: ordinary and SharedChannel synchronously reject zero ports, empty or malformed proxy hosts, missing mandatory credentials, and empty or oversized RFC 1929 fields
implementation.resolver: SOCKS endpoints remain one logical source and skip local origin resolution while allowing caller resolver configuration for other endpoints
implementation.identity: TLS SNI, certificate verification, default :authority, exporter ownership, gRPC metadata, picker identity, and retry ownership remain origin-bound
implementation.credentials: username/password bytes exist only in the RFC 1929 exchange and cannot enter the origin HPACK field block
implementation.retry: connection closure, refusal, network/host unreachable, TTL expiry, and proxy general failure enter existing endpoint backoff; authentication, protocol, and configuration errors are non-retryable
implementation.lifecycle: ordinary and SharedChannel retain their existing HTTP2 connection owner, cancellation, backoff, and shutdown paths above the tunnel

advantages_over_pinned_grpc_core: native pure-Zig authenticated SOCKS5 transport instead of HTTP CONNECT only
remote origin DNS without application resolver or hosts-file mutation
structured SOCKS protocol errors participate in endpoint retry classification
native_cases: RFC 1929 is the only offered method when downgrade is disabled
domain address type carrying localhost and the exact dynamic origin port
first proxy general failure followed by bounded endpoint backoff and successful retry
certificate-pinned TLS 1.3 and h2 through the retried tunnel
SharedChannel unary RPC through a separate authenticated tunnel
exact origin authority and absence of Proxy-Authorization metadata
caller origin resolver invocation count remains zero
HTTP CONNECT/SOCKS conflict and malformed proxy configuration fail synchronously for both owners

assertions: RFC 1929 username/password authentication is mandatory and accepted
origin target is foo.test.google.fr as SOCKS domain address
certificate verification and h2 ALPN use foo.test.google.fr
two canonical UnaryCall RPCs validate independent protobuf payload sizes
exactly one proxy tunnel carries both RPCs

verification_commands: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='gRPC Channels use authenticated SOCKS5' --summary all
zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='SOCKS5 proxy options' --summary all
remaining_gap: explicit SOCKS5 channel transport is complete; PAC and automatic SOCKS environment URI selection remain separate policy work
